entries.title: Thinkers of Cernavodă: Mysterious Stone Age figurines discovered in a 7,000-year-old grave in Romania
entries.caption:
🗿 Romania’s 7,000-year-old “Thinkers” are still a mystery.

Live Science reports that archaeologists uncovered the fired-clay pair in 1956 in a Stone Age grave at Cernavodă. One figure leans forward with his head in his hands; the other sits upright. Both are associated with the Late Neolithic Hamangia culture, around 5000 B.C.

Their purpose remains uncertain. Interpretations range from ritual or solar symbolism to mourners or a paired representation of masculine and feminine principles. None is confirmed.

Why do you think these small figures still feel so modern?

Source: Live Science (16 Nov 2026)
https://www.livescience.com/archaeology/thinkers-of-cernavoda-mysterious-stone-age-figurines-discovered-in-a-7-000-year-old-grave-in-romania

entries.title: Medieval Readers Saw Floods, Plagues and Comets as Omens of Doom—So They Created a Mysterious Manuscript of Apocalyptic Artworks to Peruse at Will
entries.caption:
Medieval readers confronting plagues and floods apparently sought solace in the terrifying art of "The Book of Miracles," a 16th-century manuscript slated for auction according to Smithsonian Smart News on November 18, 2026. This rare artifact, likely created in Augsburg, reportedly features 167 distinct paintings depicting extreme weather events and strange celestial phenomena. While scholars suggest these apocalyptic artworks served as omens of doom to be perused at will, the exact motivations of its original creators remain partially shrouded in history. Could such vivid historical expressions of collective anxiety offer unexpected comfort to modern readers facing their own unprecedented global uncertainties?

Source: Smithsonian Smart News · 18 Nov 2026

entries.title: Tiny dog. Wild ancestry.
entries.caption:
Tiny dog, unexpected family history. 🐕

A genetic study found traces of coyote ancestry in Chihuahuas, estimated at roughly 0.1% of their genome. The link appears to come from interbreeding between coyotes and ancestors of domestic dogs long ago.

That does not mean a Chihuahua is a miniature coyote. Researchers say this small genetic contribution probably does not explain the breed’s bold personality. More research is needed to pin down the ancestral connection.

Source: Smithsonian · 18 Nov 2026
https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/chihuahuas-seem-to-carry-a-tiny-bit-of-coyote-dna-but-thats-probably-not-why-they-have-fearless-personalities-180989886/
